newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Exploration firm optimistic on E.African oil find.
newsitem.headline: Exploration firm optimistic on E.African oil find.

text.p: Lonropet, an offshoot of Lonrho Plc, believed there was no reason why there should not be significant oil finds off the east coast of Africa, contrary to popular belief.

Addressing the Africa Upstream conference, Lonropet project leader Jaap Poll said that when the company began exploration work in the Rovuma Basin in Mozambique about a year ago, it quickly came across the "myths" that the east coast was gas prone and did not have oil deposits.

He said the oil and gas deposits in the Bredasdorp Basin on the South African coast, dried up oil deposits in Madagascar as well as the Pande gas fields on the Mozambican costs indicated that there was "no reason why the east coast of Africa should not have" oil deposits as well.
Most African oil has to date been found off West Africa although South Africa's Soekor and Engen are to start drilling at its E-BT field in the Bredasdorp Basin in February next year.

Lonropet, or Lonrho de Rovuma Petroleum S.A.R.L., is a focused "single purpose" exploration company relying heavily on past studies done by several oil companies as well as consultants to determine whether there is exploitable oil in the Rovuma Basin.
It has entered into a production sharing agreement with the Mozambican government and Poll said the exploration economics of the project were encouraging.
"We certainly intend to be around for quite a while," he said.
